segments: The mountains, hills, and valleys around Melitene were full of Agagrian (or Hagarene) Turkmens, who were raiding everywhere.
From a single village,
in the district of Ḥiṣn Manṣūr,
they took seven thousand oxen, cows, donkeys, and she-asses,
and forty-five thousand sheep and goats.
And they also seized the pen (sheepfold) of Mādīq, and of Mār Asyā and Mār Dīmaṭ,
and carried off from them a great amount of booty.
And that ʿAlī Bahādur pursued and drove them out of the country,
and their leader, whose name was Shūtī (Jūtī?) Beg, he captured and imprisoned in the fortress of Masara.
And while the people of Melitene were occupied in this false peace,
Baiju went forth with his forces from the inner country of Bithynia,
and they spread out during the days of Nisan into the regions of Galatia and Cappadocia.
And they began attacking the fortresses,
so that they might surrender to Rukn al-Dīn.
And they arrived at the city of Albistan,
and shed the blood of all the people who were in it,
about seven thousand,
and the boys and girls they carried off into captivity.
And they reached Melitene on Saturday, the day of the new moon of Elul.
And that Bahādur fled to Gākhtai (Gākhtī?).
Then Baiju made the people of Melitene swear allegiance to Rukn al-Dīn,
and he took from it a full load of dinars,
and left in it one of the servants of Rukn al-Dīn named Fakhr al-Dīn Ayaz,
and he himself set out towards Ḥiṣn Ziyād (Kharput),
because a command had come to him from the King of Kings, Hulegu,
that he should quickly go down to Baghdad.
And when the year 1569 entered,
[Baiju did] great [harm] to that country {OCR?}.
Because Malik Ṣāliḥ, son of Badr al-Dīn, the lord of Mosul, had in those days come from the service of Hulegu,
and Turkān, the daughter of Jalāl al-Dīn Khwarazmshah, had been given to him as a wife,
and she was with him dressed in the attire of Mongol women.
Indeed, all the inhabitants of the country fled and hid in the city,
until Baiju had passed through.
Then ʿAlī Bahādur,
as soon as Baiju Noyan had crossed the Euphrates,
returned and came to Melitene.
